issues.item: Triggers: Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident
issues.explanation: For a police trauma profile, the trigger set is not clinically coherent as a group. Physical touch can fit, but crash imagery and burnt smell together suggest a road traffic accident or fire-related trauma rather than police-related trauma, and there is no supporting memory or appraisal content tying these cues back to police trauma.

issues.item: Triggers: Olfactory Danger Cue: Burnt smell
issues.explanation: The contamination appraisal is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. It more commonly fits sexual assault or severe physical violation. Here it is unsupported by the trigger and memory items, which focus on fragmented recall and guilt rather than shame/violation themes.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: Hypervigilance towards dangerous people could occur after police trauma, but in this profile it is weakly supported because the triggers point toward accident/fire cues rather than interpersonal threat cues. This creates a cross-node mismatch between maladaptive strategy content and the rest of the selected items.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: 'Contamination/feeling dirty' is more typically coherent with sexual assault or severe bodily violation trauma. In a police-trauma profile, it is hard to reconcile this appraisal unless there are other items indicating sexualized assault, humiliating bodily violation, or related memory content, which are absent here.

A tactile trigger of general physical touch would usually imply trauma involving bodily contact/restraint. That could occur in police trauma, but in this profile there is no supporting memory or appraisal content about physical restraint, assault, or contact-based threat. Given the rest of the profile emphasizes authority/police cues, danger, mistrust, and guilt, this broad touch trigger stands out as insufficiently supported and clinically hard to place.

vignette: Sunit has been a graphic designer for over fifteen years, working from his home office in a quiet suburban neighborhood. His life took a sudden and devastating turn when he witnessed an incident involving police that left him deeply traumatized. Sunit’s trauma began on the day he was walking back home after a late meeting with a client and saw a heated confrontation between the police and a man he knew from his community. The man, someone he trusted, was in handcuffs, bleeding from a wound on his head. The scene was chaotic, with sirens blaring and officers shouting commands. Sunit tried to intervene but was forced back by the police, who were convinced he was a threat due to his attire resembling that of the suspect’s allies. Since then, certain smells and sights have triggered vivid recollections of this traumatic event. The burnt smell of the burning tires nearby on that fateful day immediately transports him back to the scene, replaying those harrowing moments over and over again in his mind. Every time he sees someone in a uniform, especially police officers, it brings back intense feelings of guilt and betrayal. When Sunit tries to make sense of what happened, he finds himself struggling with words. He knows what transpired but cannot articulate the sequence of events clearly. When he attempts to explain the encounter, his thoughts get jumbled, and he loses the thread of his narrative mid-sentence. This inability to recount the incident clearly exacerbates his feelings of guilt and mistrust. Sunit has come to believe that the world is a dangerous place where people cannot be trusted, especially those in authority. He feels betrayed by someone who was once close to him and now views every uniformed figure as a potential threat. These beliefs have led him to adopt several maladaptive strategies. Before any interaction, he meticulously rehearses what he will say, convinced that his words might incriminate or endanger him. This hypervigilance extends beyond mere thoughts; Sunit actively avoids making future plans, fearing they could be disrupted by unexpected encounters with authority figures. His mistrust has also infiltrated his professional life as a graphic designer. He often rehearses conversations with clients and colleagues, worrying about saying the wrong thing or being misunderstood. These strategies have created a reinforcing cycle of negative appraisals and triggers. The more he avoids future plans and remains vigilant for dangerous people, the stronger his feelings of mistrust and danger become. Each time he encounters an authority figure in uniform or smells something reminiscent of that day, it intensifies his memory difficulties and guilt. Sunit’s avoidance has strained his relationships with colleagues who find him distant and preoccupied. He feels increasingly isolated, unable to share his experiences due to his fear of being misunderstood or judged. The weight of these symptoms finally compelled Sunit to seek help after a particularly distressing encounter at the supermarket where he broke down in tears upon seeing a police officer. Sunit is most afraid that his fears will overwhelm him and that he won’t be able to maintain his professional life or relationships. He hopes for understanding and support, believing that with help, he might find the words to explain what happened and regain some sense of trust and safety in the world around him.
